newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WAUGH TWINS LEAD NEW SOUTH WALES FIGHTBACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH TWINS LEAD NEW SOUTH WALES FIGHTBACK.

text.p: Twins Steve and Mark Waugh shared an unfinished third wicket partnership of 139 to lead a New South Wales fightback against Queensland in their Sheffield Shield match in Brisbane on Saturday.

Showing timely form ahead of the third test between Australia and West Indies next week, Mark Waugh hit 78 not out and brother Steve 69 not out to lift New South Wales, 359 behind on first innings, to 206 for two at the close of the third day of the four-day match.
Queensland were bowled out on the stroke of lunch for 549, test wicketkeeper Ian Healy missing his first century for the state team when he fell for 88.
Paceman Andrew Bichel, who notched a career best six for 56 on Friday to enhance his test claims, followed up by hitting 58, his second Shield half century.
In Perth, a third wicket partnership of 238 between Justin Langer and Damien Martyn put Western Australia in a strong position on the second day of their match against South Australia.
Western Australia were 289 for three at the close after dismissing South Australia for 258 in their first innings.
Langer was 146 not out, with Martyn caught and bowled for 104 by paceman Jason Gillespie, who took all three Western Australian wickets to fall to finish with three for 43 from 22 overs.
